**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — Section 6.1**

The document does contain a restriction on us, despite the planner's "likely absent" hint: Section 6 ("Exclusivity") at paragraph p0037 bars the Company from participating in any project similar to the Site on the Internet for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products.

Why it does not warrant a redline:

- **Duration:** "during the term of this Agreement" only — no post-term tail, and the term is exitable on 90 days' notice (§4.1). Better than the fallback's 12-month cap. The two-year tail in §6.3 runs against **HDI**, so it benefits us and is not flagged.
- **Scope:** tied to a named product line and named competitors (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) and only to a competing *website*, not to "any competing business" — so it avoids walk-away territory. It does not restrict what we may buy or build.
- **Carve-outs:** §6.2 preserves our closeout-merchandise site, and the §1.1 definition of "Deerskin Products" excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined (minor sub-elements short of preferred): the elastic reach of "products substantially similar" / "companies similar to", and the absence of an express internal-development/acquisition carve-out.
